title: India Set To Enter Global Aircraft Manufacturing Club As Adani-Embraer Plan Regional Jet Production: Report
text:
Business
Swarajya Staff
Jan 08, 2026 | Updated 10:41 AM GMT+5:30

India is on the verge of becoming one of the few countries in the world with a final assembly line for commercial fixed-wing aircraft as the Adani group has partnered with Embraer to make the Brazilian aerospace firm's regional jets in India, Times of India reported.
These aircraft designed for short- to medium-haul operations, with seating capacities ranging from 70 to 146 passengers, are currently used by airlines across multiple global markets.
Last month, Adani Aerospace signed an MoU with Embraer in Brazil for the FAL, according to the TOI report.
With domestic airline's aircraft order books already stretching into four figures, Indian policymakers see this as the right moment to anchor aircraft assembly within the country.
The idea is simple: early customers of the India's first commercial FAL get stronger incentives, and as volumes rise, the support gradually tapers off, allowing the ecosystem to stand on its own feet.
"Several things are under consideration, including fiscal incentives for those ordering from this FAL. Like any new programme, the idea is to give incentives on a reducing basis as the orders grow, say, after every 50 orders placed," an official was quoted as saying by TOI.
Embraer is not starting from zero here. Its aircraft are already flying Indian skies, and that familiarity could give the proposed assembly line an early push.
The government reportedly hopes that the success of this FAL could encourage global aviation giants Airbus and Boeing to consider full assembly lines in India instead of limiting engagement to sourcing.
Beyond assembly, Adani Group's broader ambition is taking shape around maintenance, conversions and long-term aircraft support.
